fact: The Prime Minister, on information from the Commissioner of Police, told the National Assembly that the Crime Occurrence Tracking System is used for the management and tracking of complaints and declarations from initial reporting to final case disposal, and has been operational since 2011.

The Prime Minister, on information from the Commissioner of Police, described the Crime Occurrence Tracking System as a digital platform connecting all police stations to the main server at Police Headquarters, used on personal computers in the stations.

The Prime Minister, on information from the Commissioner of Police, said all police stations, including Moka, Saint Pierre and Quartier Militaire, are equipped with personal computers for the use of the Crime Occurrence Tracking System, which connects all stations to the headquarters server; no count of stations or of stations entering records is given.

The Crime Occurrence Tracking System is the police's own, answered for by the Commissioner of Police through the Prime Minister as Minister of Home Affairs, with the government's Central Informatics Bureau working with the police on its replacement.

The Prime Minister said the Crime Occurrence Tracking System has been enhanced but never upgraded since 2011, and that the police have initiated action to replace it entirely with a modern case management system, the Central Informatics Bureau having advised retaining a special consultant, a process then under way; no date or budget for the replacement is given.

News Moris, carrying Defi Media's account of the Prime Minister's reply in the National Assembly, reports that the Crime Occurrence Tracking System was introduced in 2011 to manage and track complaints.
The report has the Prime Minister saying all police stations are equipped with personal computers used for the Crime Occurrence Tracking System; no count of stations is given.

The report has the Prime Minister announcing that the Crime Occurrence Tracking System, improved but never replaced since 2011, is to be replaced by a new case management system, with a specialised consultant to be hired on the Central Informatics Bureau's recommendation; no date or budget for that replacement is given.
